notes.title: ‘VA-11 Hall-A: Design Works’ Opens for Pre-Orders
notes.notes:
Acclaimed boutique design studio Lost In Cult is proud to announce the upcoming release of VA-11 Hall-A: Design Works, a premium art and design book created in close collaboration with Sukeban Games and their publisher Ysbryd, the teams behind beloved cyberpunk bartending sim VA-11 Hall-A. 

Set to ship in Q2 2026, this officially licensed release dives deep into the neon-lit world of Glitch City, chronicling the entire creative journey of VA-11 Hall-A through in-depth commentary, stunning concept art, and exclusive developer insights. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25278042/fcb57ccebf66790c289e7b10276b93f5a01cfc42.png[/img]

“VA-11 Hall-A’s visual identity, storytelling, and emotional resonance make it a perfect fit for our Design Works series,” said Ryan Brown from Lost In Cult. “Almost a decade on from its debut, we’re treating this title with the respect and prestige it deserves, working closely with the original creators to craft something truly special for the fans.”

As with all entries in Lost In Cult’s acclaimed Design Works imprint, this is more than just an artbook - it’s a definitive celebration of the impact, artistry, and cultural legacy of a generation-defining indie title. 

VA-11 Hall-A: Design Works delves into the corrupt sprawl of Glitch City, exploring its culture, characters, and the iconic dive bar at the heart of the game. It offers fans a deeper understanding of the world’s creation and the cyberpunk influences that shaped it, whilst also providing a rare glimpse into the history of Venezuela - home of the development team - and the unique challenges they faced bringing their vision to life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25278042/9746ae581f661abfe32b00d9d3cd1f5bdca4e57f.jpg[/img]
In short, VA-11 Hall-A: Design Works will serve as a celebration of this beautiful indie masterpiece and the people who made it all possible, featuring contemporary interviews with writer/programmer Fernando Damas, artist/designer Christopher Ortiz, and composer Michael Kelly. 

For the first 48 hours, fans who order the Deluxe Edition will receive an exclusive bar bill bookplate signed by Sukeban Games’ very own Fernando Damas and Christopher Ortiz. To secure this signed copy, orders must be placed by 6pm BST on Saturday, April 12th, 2025.

The Deluxe Edition will only be available during the pre-order window and will not return, making it a definitive collector’s item for true VA-11 Hall-A fans.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25278042/7d8118f403ea34a5738655979bbe809467e09eb2.jpg[/img]

The Deluxe Edition, exclusive to the pre-order period, will include:
[list]
[*] A variant hardcover with exclusive artwork.
[*] A collector’s slipcase and themed housing box.
[*] The downloadable short story, Sapphic Pussy Rhapsody, written by Fernando Damas and illustrated by Merengedoll, officially printed for the very first time!
[*] Ephemera such as posters, stickers, and art cards.
[*] Early bird signed bookplates for orders placed within the first 48 hours.
[/list]
"VA-11 Hall-A was a labour of deepest love. For its medium, for its inspirations, for humanity itself," offers Fernando Damas, writer and programmer at Sukeban Games. "For such a work to be chronicled we expected nothing less than it being handled by those that love it as much as the game loves them back."

Pre-orders for both the Standard and Deluxe Editions of VA-11 Hall-A: Design Works are [b]open now[/b] at [url=www.lostincult.co.uk/va11halla]www.lostincult.co.uk/va11halla[/url] and will be available for a limited 60-day window, [b]closing on June 5th at 6pm BST[/b].

notes.title: CYBERPUNK RED X VA-11 HALL-A CROSSOVER
notes.notes:
No, your eyes do not [b]Fool[/b] you on this fine [b]April[/b] day.

Yes, this is something that [b]actually exists and you can download![/b]

[b]R Talsorian Games[/b], of the seminal [b]Cyberpunk RED[/b] fame, whose name you might’ve learned about from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1091500/Cyberpunk_2077/]a certain other award-winning Cyberpunk videogame[/url], or its related anime that [b]coincidentally also includes a small lady called Rebecca[/b]; has just released one of their many fun and interesting DLCs (free supplements of neat things you can add to your Tabletop RPG sessions) [b]and the topic this time around is your favorite depressed woman in her late 20s and her friends.[/b]

[b]Mixing Drinks–Changing Lives[/b] is a 20 pages long supplement that gives you a good idea on how to add VA-11 Hall-A characters to your Night City escapades.

Is this [b]canon[/b]? Only as canon as you want it to be with your gaming group. Which is to say… [b]not officially, no[/b]. But the R Talsorian peeps went so far above and beyond in translating the world and ideas of VA-11 Hall-A that it might as well be!

[b]It’s not, though[/b]. We wouldn’t have been able to release this sort of small and fun collab so easily or swiftly if it was.

If this got you interested [b]you should go to their website and download it![/b] And maybe grab a copy of the [b]Core Rulebook[/b] while you’re there. I also have it in good authority that their supplement [b]Black Chrome[/b] has a cheeky nod to VA-11 Hall-A for those observant enough.

The supplement
[url=https://rtalsoriangames.com/2024/04/01/cyberpunk-red-april-2024-dlc-mixing-drinks-changing-lives-va-11-hall-a-crossover/]Click here.[/url]

Their online store
[url=https://talsorianstore.com/]Click here.[/url]

And if you want a bit more detail on how this all happened, we have a blog post about it!
[url=https://sukeban.moe/index.php/2024/03/31/cyberpunk-red-x-va-11-hall-a-crossover/]Click here.[/url]

notes.title: Sukeban Games Popularity Poll 2019 Results!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25278042/d314f1770b20492f31e0801b16a37e912e689e77.png[/img]

Before starting, we want you to know that you’ve been heard! As such Fore has been honored with the Best Boy award to make up for the fact he wasn’t present in the poll in spite of unprecedented support for everyone’s favorite cat.

On March 21, 2017, we posted the results of an impromptu popularity poll that ran for a week. In that poll there were 1318 total entries among which we counted 3975 null votes and 11832 unassigned points. 

A bit short and messy.

In December of 2019 we ran another popularity poll and this time it was allowed to run for almost a month. We received a total of 17941 entries across three different language polls. This time, between them there were merely 567 null votes and 998 unassigned points.

As it turns out, properly explaining the rules in the poll itself goes a long way!

But what are these “rules”? Simple! You pick your top five characters going down in order from first to fifth favorite. Each one gets between 5 and 1 points depending on how high their position is and their final position in the poll itself depends on the sum total of these points. Duplicate votes in each entry are removed and the options are pushed up in position, with the new empty space being counted as “null” in the final tally. In this way people can vote for more than just a single favorite and the results are still reflective of how prominent in votes that character’s popularity was overall.

Now, we could jump straight into the top 10 but there’s more to tell! We were able to separate data through more means, not only through gender but also through region owing to having three separate polls: One in Chinese, one in Japanese, and one in English. It should be noted that the English poll was the only available option to participate in for a couple of hours and so a lot of people from other regions voted in it in their excitement; of note too is that the Japanese poll was actually shared by some Japanese video game media outlets, and the Chinese poll received an outpouring of support even though some of the entrants may have had to use a VPN to participate.

You’re all awesome is what we’re trying to say.

So, let’s address some of the results common to all of the polls.

[h3]The Big Three[/h3]

These are Jill, Dorothy, and Dana, in that order from first to third. They’re the most recurrent first, second, and third places across all three polls and their subsets—with the specific exception of Non-Binary and Female in the English poll, where it switches to “Jill, Dana, Dorothy” instead.

They’re even the top three most recurrent top three placements! Across all three polls the most prevalent characters for first and second favorites are Jill, Dorothy or Dana. Everyone’s third favorite position is mixed up a bit however, with in order of most common to least, “Dana, Dorothy, Jill” in both EN and CN, and “Dorothy, Jill, Dana” in JP.

[h3]The Warring Triad[/h3]

The next three spots are just as recurrent but not nearly as set. These three are Stella, Sei, and Alma. These three are recurrent in these three spots most cases with a few exceptions. In the JP Non-binary and CN Non-diclosed subsets Alma got displaced by Anna, while in the CN Non-binary subset Stella got displaced by Anna and tied with Kira☆Miki.

The order of these three in the grand total switches per region. In EN it’s “Alma, Sei, Stella”, with JP being “Stella, Alma, Sei”, and CN ordered as “Sei, Alma, Stella”. 

In EN the “Alma, Sei, Stella” order is the same in all the subsets save for Non-Binary and Others where it’s “Sei, Alma, Stella” instead. 

In JP their “Stella, Alma, Sei” order is consistent across all subsets except Non-Binary where instead its “Stella, Anna, Sei”, with Others having no patterns save for Jill being in first place.

In CN the “Sei, Alma, Stella” pattern is only kept for the Male and Others subset, whereas in all other subsets Anna displaces someone else, so we end up with “Sei, Alma, Anna” for Female, “Sei, Anna, Alma” for Non-Binary, and “Stella, Anna, Sei” for Secret.

[h3]The Battle Royale[/h3]

After these 6 spots the results start varying wildly, growing ever more wild as they go down the list. However, where a Top 10 is concerned, some names recur: Anna, Kira☆Miki, Gillian, Streaming-chan, and Rad Shiba. With the first three of those being commonplace and the rest switching and shifting and barely not making it into the top 10.

Those that just barely missed their shot at the Top 10 include Gil, Kira☆Miki, Anna, Rad Shiba, and Streaming-chan. Streaming-chan makes a comeback in JP, however, where she actually beats Kira☆Miki and leaves the dog out of the top 10. In CN, neither Streaming-chan nor Rad Shiba make it to the top 10 and it’s Betty instead who wraps up the recurrent names of Gillian, Kira☆Miki and Anna. Funnily enough, in the CN Female demographic the counter for null votes is so large it manages to displace Deal. Poor guy.

[h1]The Top 10[/h1]

Finally! The moment you’ve been waiting for: Let’s talk about the top 10 characters and what they have to say!

[h2]#10 - Rad Shiba (5828 points)[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25278042/7a8afe615320605351ed21054bda0308c8bbce6b.png[/img]

[h2]#9 - Anna (9119 points)[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25278042/61d1f084d85beb2e24f8b3feda20838d366119eb.png[/img]

[i]C̨̜̱͊͌̚q̦͝n̗͚͂͋ ̗̋ù͖͕̓j̡͛wm̛̱͈̙̽͘b̛̯u̠̾r͓̬̫̿̄͋m̡̻͕̰͍͛̋̌̈́̎n̨͕̙͔̱̾̄̅̾͆͘ͅ ͙̹̮̟̑͌̂͘x̙͎̻̀̃́ǒ͎̙̏ ̨̪̳͕̤̗̈̋͆͌̈́͘ć͍̣̻̯̘̂̆̍̎q̪͉̘̹̼̇̋̒͆̈n̡̮̫̥̋͌͘͞ ̟͔̎̀̓͟y͙̅x̡̬͚͕̀͊̑̓ǘ͈̰̱͐̀̄͢ű̺̹̩̅̒̆ͅ r̢̄ẘ͚̘̹̅̐ notes.title: Have You Played VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action?
notes.notes:
I didn t sleep well last night, but the sight of my brand new synthetic potted plant as I woke up at least made it a bit more bearable. I ve just come back from my smoke break, and I m mixing a drink called a Crevice Spike. The recipe calls for 2 Powdered Delta, 4 Flanergide, and optional Karmotrine, an alcoholic component. I ve accidentally put 14 lots of Karmotrine into the drink. My client is a 24-year-old sentient humanoid robot sex worker with the body of a 13-year-old. She s conversing with a talking Shiba Inu called Nacho Tumbleweed Jr. This is VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action, a visual novel mixed (HAHA) with a bartending minigame. Only, pretty much the whole game is bartending.

notes.title: Announcing Cyberpunk Bartender Action N1RV Ann-A! Coming in 2020
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25278042/ee456a345ae0f28d6e1caf975a68bf316a5ff424.gif[/img]


It is with great pleasure that we announce that a new game in the Cyberpunk Bartender Action series is in the works! featuring a whole new cast and new ways to play and see the story unfold.

The story this time around is about Sam, a bartender living in Saint Alicia; an artificial island that, just like Glitch City, was developed as a playground for corporations that have been forming city states of their own around the globe in order to circumvent regulations. Sam is at odds with her romantic partner, Leon, who is the head of a small Yakuza family that operates at the redlight district. Their relationship is in the rocks, as they deal with the conflicts arising from their very different lives while taking care of their 8 year-old boy, Tony, who’s growing up in a increasingly harsher society.

The game has been in development for about nine months and we decided it was in a good enough state to be shown. It will be a stand-alone game, meaning that you don’t have to play VA-11 Hall-A in order to enjoy it (but it will certainly give you insight into existing lore).  It will also feature big improvements over VA-11 Hall-A in many aspects, but you’ll have to wait a bit more to find out.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X85KOAYfObc

A lot of work has gone into this reveal so I want to thank to everyone involved in this project. It’s been a huge pleasure to go back to the world we started with Valhalla and it certainly won’t be the last title to do so!

We have a Steam page up already so you can wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/914210/N1RV_AnnA_Cyberpunk_Bartender_Action/

notes.title: VA-11 HALL-A, the cyberpunk bartender action game, is getting a sequel
notes.notes:
The cyberpunk bartender action game VA-11 HALL-A is getting a sequel, and its title is just as weird (and annoying to type) as the original. N1RV ANN-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action will feature the new adventures of a new bartender named Sam, who works at the "most iconic and luxurious bar" in the idyllic upscale paradise of Saint Alicia. 

Not all is as it appears, however, and Saint Alicia's glittering facade hides a seedy criminal underbelly, replete with extortion, trafficking, and worse. Sam's partner Leon is hip-deep in it as a member of the Yakuza, which puts a tremendous strain on their relationship. Through it all, you must serve drinks to people who will stop at almost nothing to maintain their lifestyles, not just for yourself but also your eight-year-old son, Tony. 

It sounds like N1RV ANN-A will play a lot like VA-11 HALL-A, as lives and stories will change based on which drinks are served to what customers. Relate well to your patrons and you'll unlock secrets and earn better tips that will enable you to build a better life—and maybe put all this cyberpunk bartending business behind you. 

“Most games use a big-picture perspective, but what made VA11 HALL-A special was its focus on the characters and their problems,” Sukeban Games co-founder Christopher 'Kiririn51' Ortiz said. "It’s about getting to know people on a personal level, this time with a shiny new location, more options for drink orders, and more ways to relate to customers." 

We didn't find VA-11 HALL-A all that terribly engaging, saying in our 2016 review that it tries to do interesting things, but is mainly just boring to play—although we noted that if "you long for a cyberpunk narrative you can really get your teeth into," it might do the trick. For an awful lot of players, it clearly did: User reviews on Steam are "overwhelmingly positive," and people on GOG seem to like it a lot too. N1RV ANN-A is currently expected to be out sometime in 2020.

notes.title: What game did you finish despite hating every minute of it?
notes.notes:
Videogames really end whenever you stop playing them. If you love them, maybe that's after New Game + or a replay with every character option. If you hate them, maybe that's after half an hour of frustration and a checkpoint that's on the wrong side of an unskippable cutscene. That's how it should be anyway, but sometimes we just have to see the credits of a game we're not enjoying, whether out of sheer bloody-mindedness, or because we're reviewing it and feel obliged to, or we just have to know how bad it can really get.

Hate's a strong word to use, especially for a videogame. And yet, sometimes they really do shit us to tears. This week's PCG Q&A asks the question: What game did you finish despite hating every minute of it?

Samuel Roberts: Final Fantasy XIII-2

I finally beat this Square Enix RPG last weekend, after reaching the game's finale (and one of the many endings) when I reviewed it back in 2015. Hot damn, I did not like the last few hours of that game. I went to one area to grind for hours, then returned to the final stage, overcame some terrible platforming puzzles and killed the same boss four times. There are some clever systems in FFXIII-2, like the ability to level up monsters and have them fight alongside you, a little like Pokemon. But past a certain point, the game is all busywork. It's all collectables, experience points and backtracking. I wanted it to be over so bad, and now realise why it took me over three years to return to the damn game.

Now I'm deliberating whether I want to put myself through Lightning Returns, the final game of the trilogy. The problem with XIII-2 is its characters aren't endearing to me in the way that FFX's or XV's are. This was like playing bad anime. It wasn't all bad by any means, but the finale tested my patience.

Phil Savage: Kane & Lynch 2

OK, maybe I didn't hate every minute of it. In fact, I enjoyed IO's second Kane & Lynch for its first half an hour, thanks almost entirely to its distinct presentation. Pretty soon, though, I was just hate-playing—sticking around in the vague hope that it did anything worthwhile. It did not. My overriding memory of the game was an endless procession of cover shooting, with no pacing or variety or anything to hold your interest. Just hours of crouching behind walls, shooting people, broken up only by the occasional cutscene in which the two protagonists shout at each other. The very best thing about Kane & Lynch 2 is that it's only four hours long, and so at least the misery didn't persist for long.

There remains a dedicated cadre of game critics—Andy Kelly is one of them—convinced that Kane & Lynch 2 is good. And, assuming they're not just having a mass hallucination, maybe there's something I'm just not getting about four hours of shooting a gun and nothing else. At least there was a happy end: IO returned to Hitman, which was good.

Tom Senior: Warhammer 40,000 Gladius—Relics of War

If I hate a game I never tend to finish it unless, of course, I'm reviewing it. The last review I remember turning into a grueling slog was Warhammer 40,000 Gladius—Relics of War, a well-meaning attempt to turn the Warhammer 40K universe into a 4X strategy game. You do technically explore, expand, exploit and exterminate, but the combat focus was a poor fit for a hex-based game lacking in tactical depth. The units have stat differences, technically, but that didn't seem to translate into any meaningful battlefield dilemmas. I was just shepherding dozens of units around the map hex by hex, turn by turn, and any fun I was having in the beginning faded into a haze of repetitive drudgery. In the end, I was pretty happy to get it off my hard drive.

Jarred Walton: The Crew 2

I don't normally play games that I'm not enjoying, but after doing the performance analysis of The Crew 2 and ranting about the idiocy of framerate caps, rubberbanding, and social networking as a type of point system, I kept playing it. The driving mechanics are okay I guess, once you get used to them, but in general there are just so many things I didn't like. And the storyline was like a really bad movie where I couldn't stop watching, and every time I'd lead in a race only to be passed near the finish because of a small driving error, I'd yell at my PC and at the developers. The ending was as meaningless as I'd expected. "Hooray, you're the king of Motor City, USA" or something trite like that.

Probably the real impetus for my continued play was my 8-year-old son, who wanted me to unlock all the ultimate vehicles—especially the helicopter. Then he was very upset that I couldn't use the helicopter in any races, or upgrade its components. Get used to disappointment, son. Especially in mediocre games.

Jody Macgregor: VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action

Even with the undocumented feature that lets you use keyboard instead of mouse controls, the bartending is boring. I could be generous and assume it's supposed to be, as a comment on how routine bar work is, but I don't feel generous because I didn't like the rest of the game any better—not the characters, or the writing. I stuck with it because people recommended it to me and I didn't want to let them down, but VA-11 Hall-A was really not for me.

notes.notes: Cyberpunk bartending game VA-11 Hall-A [official site], which Sin Vega quite liked, has launched a free update adding new story chapters. Well, old chapters. Renovated old chapters. With lots of dogs. The three-day prologue, released two years before the full game but kept separate from it, sees the run-down bar hosting a private party for adorable intelligent corgis with cute names and digital voiceboxes. Let me tell you, those woofy lads cannot handle their drink. … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Prologue Redux is here!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25278042/88d81f1db561c7894b5d4d30ea90981d0a18a33a.jpg[/img]

The day Corgis invaded Valhalla is now part of the full game.

Originally starring the grumpy veterinarian Betty, her personal Slave Boy™ Deal, and an army of dogs that gave Jill a mild PTSD (she actually just can’t stand dogs anymore, not really a PTSD), the Prologue episode was a small three-chapter release meant to be a test to gauge interest, get some money to fund development, and a bonus for pre-ordering all at the same time. We got tons of feedback that shaped the final product and it was key to our survival.

This content is now available inside the main game! It sports the shiny new visuals from the current engine, new story bits, extra room skins and new music from Garoad, plus awesome remixed songs from Sage​W and Senza​Fine.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25278042/04b75b0a8399407750779ce1728476d8a19dc4a2.gif[/img]

Look for this Rare Gab!

We hope you enjoy this piece of extra content, see you next time.

-Kiririn51

notes.title: Update 1.1.0.3 is now LIVE!
notes.notes:
This patch addresses the following bugs and errors:

[list]

[*][strike]This game's existence.[/strike]

[*]Nacho's beeps properly sound when he talks.

[*]Save files now show a leading zero when needed (Only shown in newly saved data, old saves will not show it).

[*]Game can now be closed with Alt+F4.

[*]Game now remembers if it should launch in full screen or not.

[*]Skip button deactivates while pressing Shift first (So puush users can send screens).

[*]Mixing keyboard shortcuts are now stable and complete.

[*]Advancing text through a gamepad is no longer possible to avoid gamepad-related bugs (Proper gamepad support will be added in a future update).

[*]Added message to the post-credits save screen to clarify that you can save New Game Plus data (dubbed HEART Data) there.

[*]New Game Plus intro talk no longer triggers if you complete the game and press New Game (You need to load the HEART data to see it, as intended).

[*]The flag for completing the shooter minigame now remains after New Game Plus.

[*]PC-9X no longer appears over everything if you fail to pay the light bill.

[*]Boss' bullets no longer remain on screen during the shmup minigame's victory sequence.

[*]Fixed assorted typos across the game

[/list]

Remember to report all bugs, typos and nitpicks at the forums!
